text.p: The Argentine government said Tuesday gross domestic product grew 2.7 percent in the first nine months of 1996, revising upward an earlier estimate of 2.0 percent growth.
The Economy Ministry said in a report that second quarter growth was revised upward to 4.8 percent from 2.6 percent.
"With this revision, and the estimate of the third quarter, GDP in the first nine months of the year registered growth of 2.7 percent," the report said.

"That means that even if GDP in the fourth quarter were to show no growth from the third quarter, and everything indicates there was, growth for 1996 would be close to 3.5 percent, far above the 3.0 percent that was projected at the beginning of the year."
The revision is based on a new estimate of industrial production in the second quarter.

"While the monthly industrial estimate showed a growth rate of 3.1 percent for the second quarter, the subsequent revision by the (official statistics agency) INDEC...shows growth of 6.9 percent in the same period," the report said.
It added that third quarter industrial production data will also be revised.
